key_insight: An algorithmic stability framework bounds expected catastrophic forgetting under SGD by linking sample-perturbation propagation and cumulative gradient alignment to training choices.
engineering_relevance: The analysis clarifies how dataset size, updates per task, task count, and learning-rate schedules—including decay restarts at task boundaries—enter forgetting bounds.
method: Decompose forgetting into intra-task and cross-task generalization gaps plus empirical forgetting.
Track sample perturbations within and across tasks under constant, intra-task decaying, and continuously decaying learning rates.
Bound empirical forgetting using cumulative gradient alignment without requiring convexity.
evidence_signal: Experiments on Split CIFAR-100 and Split MiniImageNet examine the empirical implications of the theoretical findings.
watch_item: The abstract reports upper bounds but does not establish their practical tightness or quantify experimental gains.
paper_title: Fine-Grained Analysis of Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Learning via Algorithmic Stability
